messages:
marie: quick RFC follow-up: proposing an 'optimistic-stream' model at the edge. stream bytes immediately to the client but treat final commit as optimistic until upstream durability checkpoint confirms. intent: avoid blocking long-tail generators. thoughts?
sam: sounds useful. client API unchanged?
marie: yes, only edge<->upstream gains a small handshake for commit tokens and resume tokens. client only sees a resume token if commit isn't confirmed.
alex: risk: side-effect duplication on retries. need idempotency or quarantining of side-effectful frames.
jonah: infra concerns: uncommitted bytes can spike memory usage. propose per-tenant caps + spill-to-disk and TTL for uncommitted state.
ruth: SLO split: keep first-byte latency low; expose commit latency separately. default = best-effort commit; customers can opt into strict commit via header.
sam: test plan: create synthetic hooks to detect duplicate side-effects and run chaos where checkpoint ACKs are dropped. gating: duplicates == 0, resume_success_rate >= 99.5%.
deploy-bot: canary started: edge/optimistic-stream v1 -> 5% for 48h. logs to infra-telemetry.
marie: thanks. next: I'll draft the short design note and add config knobs (timeout, max_uncommitted_bytes, spill threshold, resume window). alex -> duplication tests; jonah -> spill + caps; ruth -> dashboards.
